title: How to Design a Good API and Why it Matters
claim: Advocates early caller examples, explicit contracts and programmatic access to diagnostic information.
limitations: Expert experience, not comparative experiment; historic platform advice.

title: Rust API Guidelines: Type safety
claim: Distinct types clarify interpretation; builders can support complex construction.
limitations: A wrapper type alone does not validate every underlying value.

title: Rust API Guidelines: Future proofing
claim: Visibility and extension points constrain evolution; passive data structs are an explicit public-field exception.
limitations: Some examples are historical; no universal getter or sealing requirement.

title: RFC1105: API evolution
claim: Separates semantic-version categories from every possible downstream break and acknowledges behavioral-policy limits.
limitations: Not a current language specification; some described features were then unimplemented.

title: Cargo Book: SemVer Compatibility
locator: Introduction; enum variants; trait additions; non_exhaustive changes
claim: Compatibility depends on caller usage; adding exhaustive variants and later restricting construction can break clients.
context: Current guidance retrieved on research date.
limitations: Mostly compilation compatibility; runtime effects still require judgment.

title: Rust1.81 I/O contracts and implementations
claim: Default exact reads loop; slice specialization differs on failure within an explicitly unspecified buffer contract.
limitations: No execution; selected paths, not all reader implementations.

title: Rust1.81 I/O test callers
claim: Tests call chained readers and slices; short slice input asserts untouched destination.
limitations: Tests were not run; observed test expectation is not a universal API promise.

title: Working with Errors in Go1.13
locator: Whether to Wrap; Errors and package APIs
claim: Wrapping exposes machine-inspectable errors and therefore creates a caller-facing commitment.

title: Proposal: Go2 Error Inspection
claim: Motivates richer error inspection for people and programs.
limitations: Proposed details must not be assumed to match the shipped library.

title: Go1.23 errors inspection and test callers
claim: Is traverses unary and multi-error trees; Unwrap itself handles only unary form.
limitations: Read only; custom matching can affect results; no runtime test receipt.

title: Go1.23 fmt.Errorf implementation and external-package tests
claim: Formatter selects plain, unary-wrapper or multi-wrapper errors; tests distinguish text and inspectable shape.
limitations: No execution; diagnostics and programmatic identity are distinct.

title: Protobuf proto3: message evolution and unknown fields
locator: Updating A Message Type; Unknown Fields; Retaining Unknown Fields
claim: Binary compatibility differs from source compatibility; unknown fields can be lost through JSON or field-wise copying.
context: Schema evolution across independently updated readers.
limitations: Does not guarantee application semantics or each runtime configuration.

title: Protobuf Field Presence application note
claim: Explicit zero and absent differ; implicit-presence relays can erase explicit presence.
context: Patch semantics and mixed-version round trips.
limitations: Documented semantics; presence implementation not independently tested.

title: ProtoJSON Format
locator: Non-goals; unknown fields; JSON Wire Safety; JSON Options
claim: Names and unknown-field handling make JSON evolution different from binary evolution.
limitations: Defaults/options vary by implementation; only selected Go parser branches checked.

title: Protobuf-Go1.34.2 binary/JSON decode implementations
claim: Binary slow path retains unknown bytes unless discarded; JSON unknown fields error or are skipped.
limitations: Generated binary fast paths were not audited; no execution.

title: Protobuf-Go1.34.2 decode fixtures and caller tests
locator: testmessages L1054-1079; decode L24-60; JSON tests L1554-1558,L2539-2552
claim: Fixtures distinguish retained/discarded unknown binary data and rejected/skipped JSON fields.
limitations: Read only; no end-to-end mixed-version deployment or semantic-preservation proof.

title: Hyrum's Law
claim: Observed consumers can depend on undocumented behavior, complicating implementation migration.
limitations: Observation, not an impossibility proof that forbids all changes.

title: AIP180: Backwards compatibility
locator: Guidance; three compatibility types; scope note; semantic/default changes
claim: Separates source, wire and semantic compatibility and scopes strict guidance to independently updated public clients.
limitations: Policy, not universal requirement for co-deployed internal code.
